GENERAL INFORMATION

Report ID: FAI-2010-001
Mine ID: 4601731
Operation: Kestrel Ridge Mine
Date of Accident: January 11, 2010
Date of Report: May 11, 2010
Accident Classification: Fall of roof or back
Source of Injury: Roof or back
Mining Method: Room and pillar
Equipment: Roof bolter
Subunit: Underground
Activity: Ground support installation
Degree of Injury: FATALITY

DESCRIPTION OF THE ACCIDENT

The crew was installing secondary ground support along the number four entry after a routine inspection identified a change in the immediate roof. The task had been planned at the pre-shift meeting and the crew held a current permit for ground support installation. The exclusion zone under unsupported back was reduced by verbal agreement rather than by a revision to the ground control plan. A section of the immediate roof detached and the bolter operator was struck.

INVESTIGATION OF THE ACCIDENT

The investigation considered the adequacy of supervision on the shift. The supervisor held the statutory appointment required for the activity, had conducted the pre-shift briefing, and had visited the work area earlier in the shift. Communications equipment was tested and found to be serviceable throughout.

DISCUSSION

The investigation considered the adequacy of supervision on the shift. The supervisor held the statutory appointment required for the activity, had conducted the pre-shift briefing, and had visited the work area earlier in the shift. Communications equipment was tested and found to be serviceable throughout.
Investigators reviewed prior events of the same character at this and other operations. See Accident Investigation Report Document No. 2100141, September 21, 2008.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS

Root cause: Management policies and procedures did not require a geotechnical assessment before the supported line was advanced under changed roof conditions. Corrective action was directed accordingly.

CONCLUSION

The accident occurred because the exclusion zone under unsupported back was reduced by verbal agreement rather than by a revision to the ground control plan. The recurrence condition recurs wherever a person can occupy ground under a back whose support standard has been varied without a geotechnical assessment.
